## 1 Abstract

Perez-Elizalde et al. (2012, Section 3.2) analysed the second year of
the maize trial with the first year as prior and all 11 bilinear terms.
This vignette repeats their analysis and compares it with Table B.1 (the
38 linear effects), Table 2 (\\\sigma\\, the singular values and the
significant scores) and Figure 4 (the biplot).

## 2 The fit

The paper used two chains of 20,000 iterations. Here two chains of 5000
after a burn-in of 1000 suffice for the comparison.

``` r

fm <-
  bayes_ammi(
      .data       = cultivo2009
    , .y          = y
    , .gen        = entry
    , .env        = site
    , .rep        = rep
    , .nIter      = 5000
    , .prior_data = cultivo2008
    , .n0         = NULL
    , .model      = "AMMI"
    , .k          = NULL
    , .burnin     = 1000
    , .thin       = 1
    , .chains     = 2
    , .priors     = bys_priors(
          mu_mean     = 0
        , mu_var      = 1e+8
        , tau_mean    = 0
        , tau_var     = 1e+8
        , delta_mean  = 0
        , delta_var   = 1e+8
        , lambda_mean = 0
        , lambda_var  = 1e+8
        , nu          = 1
        , s2          = NULL
        )
    , .level      = 0.95
    , .seed       = 2012
    , .align      = TRUE
    , .waic       = TRUE
    )
```

``` r

s <- fm$summary
c(max_rhat = max(s$rhat), min_ess_linear = min(s[block %in% c("mu", "tau", "delta"), ess]))
```

          max_rhat min_ess_linear
          1.004002    9162.831481 

## 3 Table B.1: the linear effects

``` r

pub <- utils::read.csv(file = system.file("extdata", "perez2012.csv", package = "baystability"))
pos <- c("mu", sprintf("tau[%d]", 1:12), sprintf("delta[%d]", 1:25))
lin <- s[block %in% c("mu", "tau", "delta")]
b1 <- data.table::data.table(
    parameter = c("mu", sprintf("alpha%d", 1:12), sprintf("beta%d", 1:25))
  , published = pub$mean[match(x = pos, table = pub$parameter)]
  , here      = round(x = lin$mean, digits = 1)
  , sd_pub    = pub$sd[match(x = pos, table = pub$parameter)]
  , sd_here   = round(x = lin$sd, digits = 2)
  )
b1[, diff_in_sd := round(x = (here - published) / sd_pub, digits = 3)]
b1
```

All 38 posterior means agree with the published ones to within 0.035
posterior standard deviations, and the standard deviations agree too.

### 3.1 Why the posterior means are averages of the two years

With \\n_0 = B = 3\\ the earlier trial weighs as much as the new one, so
the posterior mean of every linear effect is the average of its two
least-squares estimates:

``` r

both <-
  bys_ls_means(
      .data = rbind(
          cultivo2008[c("site", "rep", "entry", "y")]
        , cultivo2009[c("site", "rep", "entry", "y")]
        )
    , .y    = y
    , .gen  = entry
    , .env  = site
    )
c(average_mu = both$grand_mean, published = 3848)
```

    average_mu  published
      3848.275   3848.000 

## 4 Table 2: the residual standard deviation and the singular values

``` r

sig <- sqrt(unlist(fm$tau1))
lam <- s[block == "lambda"]
t2 <- data.table::data.table(
    parameter = c("sigma", sprintf("lambda%d", 1:11))
  , published = pub$mean[match(x = c("sigma", sprintf("lambda[%d]", 1:11)), table = pub$parameter)]
  , here      = round(c(mean(sig), lam$mean))
  , sd_pub    = pub$sd[match(x = c("sigma", sprintf("lambda[%d]", 1:11)), table = pub$parameter)]
  , sd_here   = round(c(sd(sig), lam$sd))
  )
t2[, ratio := round(x = here / published, digits = 2)]
t2
```

The residual standard deviation agrees: 1305.2 against 1311.00, 0.15
posterior standard deviations apart.

The singular values do not agree: here they are 1.33 to 2.07 times the
published ones. By eq. 2.15 the posterior mean of \\\lambda_k\\ is close
to \\(n_0\lambda\_{0k} + B\\\va_k^\top\mY\vg_k)/(n_0 + B)\\. Here
\\\lambda\_{01} =\\ 5306 is the first singular value of the first year.
With equal weights, a published \\\lambda_1 = 2572\\ below
\\\lambda\_{01}/2 =\\ 2653 would need \\\va_1^\top\mY\vg_1\\ to be
negative on average, that is, the second-year data pulling the first
term against itself. The leading published values are close to
\\\lambda\_{0k}/2\\, as if the second year added nothing to them.

Two explanations were checked with the sampler of this package
(`dev/lambda-checks.R` in the source) and neither gives the published
values:

- Score columns that do not move (no pair moves, as in the
  column-by-column sampler of the paper), started at the first year’s
  fit or at random orthonormal scores: \\\lambda_1\\ is then 3613 or
  3313, not 2572, because the environment scores still follow the data.
- A prior mean of zero for the singular values with the same weight:
  \\\lambda_1\\ is then 1203.

The linear effects and \\\sigma\\, which come from the same draws, are
reproduced; the sampler gives the same draws as an independent R version
of eq. 2.15 and recovers the true values of simulated trials (validation
vignette). The published singular values therefore disagree with the
method as the paper states it, and the difference lies in the article,
through a step it does not report or an error in its Table 2, rather
than in the package.

## 5 Table 2: the significant scores

The paper lists the scores whose bivariate 0.95 HPD region excludes the
origin: genotype 12 on the second term and environments 5, 9, 23 and 25
on the first.

``` r

sc <- s[block %in% c("alpha", "gamma") & axis %in% 1:2]
sc[(block == "alpha" & label == levels(factor(cultivo2009$entry))[12]) |
     (block == "gamma" & label %in% c("5", "9", "23", "25")), list(
         parameter
       , axis
       , mean
       , sd
       , lower
       , upper
       )]
```

On the first term the environment scores agree in sign and size with the
published values (0.288, -0.277, 0.278 and 0.459 for environments 5, 9,
23 and 25; here 0.324, -0.257, 0.197, 0.505). Terms beyond the first are
weakly identified when 11 terms of similar size are fitted: their order
and orientation can differ between analyses.

## 6 Figure 4: the biplot

``` r

bp <-
  bayes_ammi_biplot(
      fit           = fm
    , burnin        = 0
    , thin          = 1
    , pb            = c(0.10, 0.05)
    , plot_stable   = FALSE
    , plot_unstable = TRUE
    , ncolors       = 5
    , .which        = "both"
    , .grid         = 100
    )
bp$biplot
```
